claims.claim: BERT-Base and BERT-Large use about 110M and 340M parameters and original pretraining uses BooksCorpus and English Wikipedia.
claims.verification_note: Original paper scale, corpora and sequence-length schedule.

claims.claim: Original BERT uses short 128-token sequences for 90% of steps and 512 tokens for the last 10%.
claims.verification_note: This condition prevents assuming every step has length 512.

claims.claim: RoBERTa changes data sources, batch, masking and training duration, confounding attribution of final quality to data size alone.
claims.verification_note: Different factors move together in the full recipe.

claims.claim: Hoffmann et al. derive compute-optimal parameter and training-token scaling for autoregressive language models.
claims.verification_note: The approximately 20 tokens/parameter rule is not an Encoder-specific benchmark.

claims.claim: ModernBERT reports training on approximately 2 trillion tokens and native 8192 context.
claims.verification_note: Training token count is distinguished from unique corpus bytes.

claims.claim: The C≈6ND formula is a simplified Transformer training compute approximation, not exact measured Encoder FLOPs.
claims.verification_note: Article explicitly marks the formula as rough modeling.
